summary.headline: Meghmani Organics Q2 FY27 standalone revenue rose 18% YoY to INR658 crore, but EBITDA was flat at INR70.9 crore as input and logistics costs squeezed margins.
summary.overview: Standalone revenue grew 18% YoY and 26% QoQ, while EBITDA stayed flat at INR70.9 crore and net profit rose 6% YoY to INR45 crore as input and logistics costs spiked and realisations stayed broadly flat. Consolidated revenue was INR666 crore (+16% YoY) with EBITDA up 40% to INR73 crore and margin of 11% versus 9%. Crop Protection margin fell to about 11% from the 19-20% reported in Q1 per analyst recollection, and management said the 15-17% target is a long-term aim. Titanium dioxide operations remain suspended, with the anti-dumping duty re-imposed on 24 October 2026 but restart still uneconomic due to sulfuric acid prices at 7-8x normal. Receivables rose sharply, with collection days moving to about 125+ from a 100-110 norm.

financial_highlights.change: +40% YoY; margin vs 9% a year ago

segments.name: Crop Protection
segments.commentary: About 75% of Q2 revenue; revenue about INR496 crore, EBITDA INR54 crore (margin about 11%), production about 10,000 MT, capacity utilisation 72%.

segments.name: Pigment
segments.commentary: About 25% of Q2 revenue; revenue INR161 crore, EBITDA INR16 crore (margin about 10%), production 4,252 MT, utilisation 51%. Exports about 75-80% of segment sales.

segments.name: Crop Nutrition
segments.commentary: Nano DAP, Nano NPK and Nano Zinc production started at the Sanand facility; no segment financials were given in the call.

segments.name: Titanium dioxide
segments.commentary: Operations remain suspended on uneconomic raw material costs; restart not commercially viable at present.

guidance_outlook: Crop Protection: double-digit top-line growth over the next 2-3 years, with long-term EBITDA margin target of 15-17%.
Pigment: top line expected at INR600-650 crore with no significant growth; EBITDA margin target of about 10-11%.
Crop Nutrition: double-digit growth over about 3 years with EBITDA margin of 20-22%, per management.
Consolidated EBITDA margin long-term target of about 13-14%.
Receivable days expected to stay within 110-115 days, against 125+ days currently.
Management expects logistics costs to normalise over the next few months; raw material costs are expected to ease if the Middle East conflict subsides.
capex_capacity: Titanium dioxide plant remains suspended; management is exploring strategic options for the asset, including partnerships or divestment, with no timeline given.
Crop Protection capacity utilisation 72% in Q2; management did not give a target utilisation level.
Nano fertiliser products (Nano DAP, Nano NPK, Nano Zinc) commenced production at the existing Sanand facility.
Pipeline of product registrations extends up to 2031; exports to more than 70 countries.
NCLT approved the amalgamation of Kilburn Chemicals Limited and Meghmani Crop Nutrition Limited into Meghmani Organics Limited.
demand_pricing: Crop Protection price pass-through has been difficult because of volatile raw material costs and an uneven customer response; Q1 saw some price increases that could not be repeated in Q2.
Crude-linked raw materials, coal, energy and utility costs rose sharply in Q2, and logistics costs were a major additional factor.
Pigment segment has passed on raw material increases so far, per management.
Europe demand is weak and the agrochemical business there is under 1% of sales; US pigment demand is currently good with no tariff impact this year.
Management said realisation per tonne is not a meaningful measure because of product mix; EBITDA percentage is the preferred metric.
Byproduct and co-product sales are below 1% of revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Why did trade receivables rise by about INR220 crore, and when will they normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it extended more credit to support customers in a challenging market. Collection days rose to about 125+ from 100-110, and are expected to stay around 110-115 days.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Crop Protection margin fall to about 11% from the earlier guidance of 15-17%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited raw material inflation, crude-linked inputs, energy and coal costs, and logistics costs. It said the 15-17% margin remains the long-term target, and that the Q1 gain partly reflected low-cost inventory.

qa_highlights.question: Is a TiO2 partnership or divestment being considered?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is exploring all options for the asset but market conditions remain challenging, and it will update investors if conditions improve.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the change in Q2 revenue growth and margins, and how much came from currency?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the growth reflects currency movement over the past year plus product mix, with better-realisation formulations and technical products. Per management, the Q2 margin was affected by input costs.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for Nano urea and Crop Nutrition margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Nano urea works as a supplement to urea rather than a full replacement, and field guidance is being used to drive adoption. Crop Nutrition is expected to grow with EBITDA margin of 20-22% over 3 years.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company pay dividends?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said dividends were paid regularly in the past but cash flow was volatile over the last 2-3 years. Dividends will be considered if the market improves and cash flow is adequate.

risks_watch: Working capital: receivable days at about 125+ against a 100-110 norm, which ties up cash and raises credit risk.
Raw material and logistics cost volatility linked to the Middle East conflict and crude oil; Crop Protection margin pass-through remains difficult.
TiO2 restart economics depend on sulfuric acid prices (7-8x normal) and on sustained anti-dumping protection.
Europe demand weakness and regulatory risk for pigments and agrochemicals.
Nano urea adoption and field-level acceptance, with negative media commentary noted by management.
Consolidated EBITDA margin of 11% in Q2 versus the 13-14% long-term target.
summary.management_tone: Cautious on near-term profitability, citing input, energy and logistics cost pressure, but confident on the long-term 15-17% Crop Protection margin and double-digit growth. Management was evasive on TiO2 restart timing and on Crop Protection price recovery, and gave no quantified near-term guidance.
key_quotes: While the near -term cost environment remains challenging, we are taking focused measures to optimize our pro duct mix, enhance operating efficiencies and strengthen profitability.
Considering these factors, restarting operations is not commercially viable.
So, in the near term, it looks a little difficult.
But on the long-term perspective, we are very optimistic to bring back the profitability for the Crop Protection segment in the range of 15% to 17%.

rows.label: Margin expansion

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Crop Protection utilisation is only 72% and Pigment 51%, and no new plant or line is guided; the only addition is Nano fertiliser production at the existing Sanand facility with no size given.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Crop Protection is guided to double-digit top-line growth over 2-3 years, but no volume target is given, Pigment is guided flat at INR600-650 crore, and Crop Protection utilisation is 72%.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is 72% in Crop Protection and 51% in Pigment, well below the 80% level that would prompt a capex announcement, and TiO2 is suspended with only divestment or partnership options under review.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management gave no quantified near-term guidance, Pigment revenue guidance was cut to INR600-650 crore, and Crop Protection margin fell to about 11% against the 15-17% long-term target.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Consolidated EBITDA margin is 11% against a 13-14% long-term target, the Pigment range was already cut, and receivable days at 125+ are above the 110-115 expected range.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Nano DAP, Nano NPK and Nano Zinc have started production at Sanand, and management guides Crop Nutrition at 20-22% EBITDA margin over about 3 years, though no sales size is given.

rows.label: Receivable days normalisation to 110-115
rows.why: Collection days rose to 125+ from a 100-110 norm after about INR220 crore of receivables build, and management expects them to stay within 110-115 days.

rows.label: Debt repayment and dividend revival
rows.why: About INR64 crore of debt was repaid by 30 Sep 2026 and standalone D/E is 0.27x, but dividends depend on cash flow, which management called volatile and will consider only if the market improves.

rows.label: TiO2 restart or divestment
rows.why: Operations are suspended, sulfuric acid is at 7-8x normal, and management gave no timeline for a partnership or divestment, saying conditions remain challenging.
